title: Monetary Policy
welcome_lead: Central banks steer the economy by adjusting interest rates and money supply.
meta_desc: A-Level Macroeconomics: monetary policy and transmission.
final_note: Monetary policy is powerful but slow - and unevenly distributed.

When low rates fail to stimulate borrowing.

walkthroughs.body_html: The main tool is the bank rate; in crisis the bank also uses QE and forward guidance. Higher rates slow borrowing and spending; lower rates do the reverse.
Rate changes feed through borrowing costs, asset prices, exchange rates and expectations. Effects take 12 to 24 months - policy must be set looking ahead.
In a liquidity trap, very low rates do not boost borrowing because confidence is too low. Japan in the 1990s and Europe after 2008 both struggled to escape.
